body.text: A commercial airliner made of cardboard to cut costs

nodes.title: Pressurization hoop strength
nodes.statement: Triple-wall cardboard fuselage skin carries the cruise pressurization hoop stress.
nodes.rationale: Pressurization sizes fuselage skin. If hoop stress exceeds cardboard strength the fuselage bursts on first cruise climb.

params.name: fuselage_radius_m
params.source: Airbus A320 fuselage diameter ~4 m handbook

check.description: Thin-wall hoop stress p*R/t compared to cardboard tensile strength.
check.code: const stress = p.pressure_diff_kpa*1000*p.fuselage_radius_m/(p.skin_thickness_mm/1000)/1e6; return {value: stress, limit: p.cardboard_tensile_strength_mpa, unit: 'MPa', pass: stress <= p.cardboard_tensile_strength_mpa, detail: `Hoop stress ${stress.toFixed(1)} MPa vs cardboard strength ${p.cardboard_tensile_strength_mpa} MPa`};

nodes.title: Wing limit load capacity
nodes.statement: Cardboard wing spar box carries the 2.5 g limit bending load without crushing.
nodes.rationale: Wings must carry 2.5g limit load without collapse. Cardboard crush strength is orders below aluminum, so spars would buckle.

params.name: load_factor
params.source: FAR Part 25 limit maneuver load factor 2.5g

check.description: Limit-load compressive stress in idealized spar caps compared to cardboard edge-crush strength.
check.code: const load = p.mtow_kg*p.gravity_m_s2*p.load_factor/p.spar_cap_area_m2/1e6; return {value: load, limit: p.cardboard_compressive_strength_mpa, unit: 'MPa', pass: load <= p.cardboard_compressive_strength_mpa, detail: `Spar stress ${load.toFixed(1)} MPa vs cardboard ${p.cardboard_compressive_strength_mpa} MPa`};

nodes.title: Moisture resistance
nodes.statement: Cardboard retains certified strength and stiffness after rain, humidity and condensation.
nodes.rationale: Airliners sit in rain, de-icing fluid and 90% humidity. Cellulose wicks water and loses most stiffness, so shape and buckling capacity vanish.

check.description: Compare wet strength retention to minimum needed for certified structure.
check.code: const retained = p.wet_retention_ratio; return {value: retained, limit: p.required_retention_ratio, unit: 'fraction', pass: retained >= p.required_retention_ratio, detail: `Wet retention ${retained} vs required ${p.required_retention_ratio}`};

nodes.title: Fire certification
nodes.statement: Uncoated cardboard cabin and structure passes airliner fire, smoke and burn-through certification.
nodes.rationale: Certification forbids readily flammable structure and interiors. Cardboard is fuel and cannot get a type certificate unprotected.

params.name: max_burn_time_s
params.source: FAR 25.853 12-second vertical burn test limit 15 s

nodes.title: Fatigue life
nodes.statement: Cardboard fuselage survives 60000 pressurization cycles without fatigue failure.
nodes.rationale: Pressurization, vibration and creep delaminate paper fibers quickly. A 100-cycle life would ground the aircraft daily.

params.name: required_cycles
params.source: Airbus A320 design service goal ~60000 flights

check.description: Compare cardboard fatigue life under cyclic humidity and pressurization to airliner design life.
check.code: return {value: p.cardboard_endurance_cycles, limit: p.required_cycles, unit: 'cycles', pass: p.cardboard_endurance_cycles >= p.required_cycles, detail: `Cardboard ${p.cardboard_endurance_cycles} cycles vs required ${p.required_cycles}`};

nodes.title: Lifecycle cost saving
nodes.statement: Cardboard airframe replacement cost stays below aluminum cost per flight.
nodes.rationale: Cheap material does not mean cheap airplane if moisture, fatigue and damage force replacement every 100 flights plus inspections.

check.description: Amortized airframe cost per flight for cardboard versus aluminum.
check.code: const alu = p.aluminum_airframe_cost_usd/p.aluminum_life_flights; const card = p.cardboard_airframe_cost_usd/p.cardboard_life_flights; return {value: card, limit: alu, unit: 'USD/flight', pass: card <= alu, detail: `Cardboard $${card.toFixed(0)}/flight vs aluminum $${alu.toFixed(0)}/flight`};

body.summary: A cardboard airliner is not feasible: cardboard is far too weak for pressurization and wing loads, collapses when wet, burns, fatigues in ~100 cycles, and would cost more per flight than aluminum.

result.detail: Hoop stress 12.0 MPa vs cardboard strength 7 MPa
Spar stress 8.6 MPa vs cardboard 5 MPa

nodes.title: Cabin pressure differential load
nodes.statement: Cruise cabin-to-ambient differential pressure does not exceed 60 kPa.
nodes.rationale: Hoop stress scales directly with differential pressure. If cruise differential exceeds 60 kPa the computed burst margin is unconservative.

nodes.title: Cardboard tensile capacity
nodes.statement: Triple-wall corrugated board provides at least 7 MPa tensile strength in the hoop direction when dry.
nodes.rationale: Cardboard strength is the allowable that hoop stress is compared against. Published linerboard values are single-digit MPa and drop sharply with moisture, so 7 MPa is optimistic.

nodes.title: Fuselage size and skin thickness
nodes.statement: Commercial fuselage needs 2 m radius with only 10 mm of load-bearing cardboard skin thickness.
nodes.rationale: Hoop stress scales with radius and inversely with thickness. A smaller radius or much thicker skin could lower stress, but 2 m radius and 10 mm skin represent a commercial 6-abreast fuselage with practical board thickness.

params.name: fuselage_radius_m
params.source: Airbus A320 fuselage diameter ~4 m handbook

nodes.title: Thin-wall hoop stress law
nodes.statement: Thin-wall hoop membrane stress equals differential pressure times radius divided by thickness.
nodes.rationale: Pressurization claim rests on membrane equilibrium sigma = p*r/t. With r/t = 200 the thin-wall formula applies, predicting about 12 MPa stress which already exceeds cardboard strength.

params.name: thin_wall_threshold_ratio
params.source: Gere and Goodno Mechanics of Materials thin-wall criterion r/t > 10

check.description: Checks thin-wall applicability r/t against threshold; if valid, sigma = p*r/t governs burst.
check.code: const r_mm = p.fuselage_radius_m * 1000; const ratio = r_mm / p.skin_thickness_mm; return {value: ratio, limit: p.thin_wall_threshold_ratio, unit: "ratio", pass: ratio >= p.thin_wall_threshold_ratio, detail: "r/t = " + ratio.toFixed(1) + " vs minimum " + p.thin_wall_threshold_ratio + " for sigma = p*r/t"};

body.summary: Pressurization burst rests on a 60 kPa load, 2 m commercial radius with 10 mm skin, only ~7 MPa cardboard strength, and the sigma = p*r/t law that predicts ~12 MPa stress and failure.

result.detail: r/t = 200.0 vs minimum 10 for sigma = p*r/t
